entities.text: Kandipati Ravi vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
1
 The Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Tirumala Devi Eada
 Criminal Petition No.8582 Of 2025
Order:

This Criminal Petition is filed by the petitioner - accused seeking to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.664 of 2024 on the file of the learned Principal Junior Civil Judge, Mahabubabad, registered for the offences under Sections 420 and 494 of the Indian Penal Code (for short "IPC").
2.
Heard the submissions of Sri B. Balaji, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Jithender Rao Veeramalla, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for respondent No.1 - State.

3. The learned petitioner counsel has submitted that the petitioner herein is facing third round of litigation and that earlier a complaint under Section 498-A and also Section 494 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry and Prohibition Act has been filed which was numbered C.C.No.86 of 1996 and wherein the petitioner herein was acquitted vide Orders dated 07.09.2000.
Again the petitioner has lodged the present complaint with the same set of allegations under Section 420 and 494 of IPC after lapse of 15 years.

He further submitted that it amounts to double jeopardy and that he cannot be prosecuted for the same allegations again and that he has filed a Divorce Petition, which was dismissed and he has preferred CMA which is pending, just bearing grudge against the petitioner herein, the present complaint is again lodged by the de- facto complainant.
Hence, he prayed to dismiss the same.
4. Inspite of service of notice, learned counsel for the respondent failed to appear before this Court.
5. The learned Additional Public Prosecutor has not disputed the fact submitted by the petitioner counsel.

The record reveals the order, date 07.09.2000 in C.C.No.86 of 1996 ending in acquittal of the petitioner herein for the charges under Sections 498-A, 494 of IPC and also Sections 3 & 4 of Dowry and Prohibition Act.
The present petition is lodged under Section 420 and 494 of the IPC with the similar allegation that was alleged in C.C.No.86 of 1996.
Therefore, the continuation of proceedings would amount to abuse of process of law.
Hence, it is a fit case to quash the proceedings.

8. In the result, the Criminal Petition is allowed, and the proceedings against the petitioner in C.C.No.664 of 2024 on the file of the learned Principal Junior Civil Judge, Mahabubabad is hereby Kandipati Ravi vs The State Of Telangana on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114139565/
1 quashed.
